runs.title: First light: finding planets we already know about
Fifteen strangers from sector 70
Calibration, round two: four sectors at once
Sector 80: a star with an orbit inside it
Sector 88: one signal gets through
Deep dive on TIC 232022864: the signal fades
Sector 88, second draw: three candidates in, three out, plus an eccentric eclipsing binary
Deep dive on TIC 373846934: 27 sectors, and the star itself is varying
Deep dive on TIC 219144734: the 19.6-day signal doesn't come back
Deep dive on TIC 349890276: it repeats, but twice per cycle
Sector 88, third draw: two candidates in, two out, and a faint 12-day lead
Deep dive on TIC 148231397: the 2.5-day signal fades, a shaky 12-day one appears
Deep dive on TIC 184512118: same period, plus a telltale second dip
Second look at TIC 148231397: the 12-day signal fails the noise test
Sector 88, fourth draw: 50 stars, three near-misses, and a neighbour's eclipsing binary
Deep dive on TIC 279950870: three dips per cycle means a wobbling star
Deep dive on TIC 271785710: an orbit that would sit inside a red giant
Deep dive on TIC 278866220: the dip belongs to the eclipsing binary next door
Sector 88, fifth draw: one bright-star candidate, gone on a second look
Deep dive on TIC 96796224: the 18-day dip doesn't come back
